text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CENTRAL BANK LOWERS MINI-BAND 0.28 PERCENT

The Central Bank lowered the reais-dollar mini-band 0.28 percent, the biggest one-day drop since March 1996, when it was lowered 0.30 percent. Analysts said the move was made because time was running out to achieve the standard 0.60 percent monthly depreciation and to encourage soy exporters to carry out foreign exchange transactions before the end of the month.
-- BRAZIL AND U.S. TRYING TO RESOLVE AUTO DISPUTE
Brazil and the United States are trying to resolve an existing dispute over Brazil's auto import policy before President Bill Clinton visits South America in May.
-- CURRENT ACCOUNT DEFICIT HITS 3.5 PERCENT OF GDP
Brazil's current account deficit in the 12-month period through the end of February hit $27 billion, or 3.55 percent of gross domestic product. Foreign reserves, however, rose to $58.5 billion.
O GLOBO
-- BANCO VETOR RENTED CAR FOR WIFE OF SAO PAULO MAYOR
Banco Vetor, a brokerage house under investigation in a multi-million dollar bond scandal, paid some 2,600 reais to rent a car for the wife of Sao Paulo Mayor Celso Pitta.
-- BRAZIL JUDGE TO ASK ITALIAN COURT TO HELP INVESTIGATION

A judge will ask an Italian court to lift secrecy rules to allow Brazilian officials to investigate bank accounts of Paulo Cesar Farias, the late aide to former President Fernando Collor. The accounts are the subject of a probe into a multi-million dollar corruption scandal.
-- CARDOSO TO SPEAK AT RIO ENVIRONMENTAL CONFERENCE
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso will address delegates at the Rio + 5 environmental conference today. Cardoso will discuss the state's role in protecting the environment.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- CRIME RATE FALLS IN SAO PAULO
Crime rates fell during Operation Centro, an anti-violence campaign launced between Feb 18 and March 3. Incidences of various crimes fell between four percent and 67 percent in the two-week period.
-- COOKING GAS PRICES TO RISE BY 9.89 PERCENT
Cooking gas prices throughout Brazil will rise by an average of 9.89 percent today, the first hike since August of last year.
-- NEW LIVER TRANSPLANT TECHNIQUE DISCOVERED
Doctors at Clinicas Hospital in Sao Paulo have discovered a new liver transplant technique that benefits people who are carrying a virus that causes cancer and who have only about six months to live.
* Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
((--John Miller, Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 248-5414))
